1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
data(starwars)
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color)) + geom_bar() 
```


3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color)) + geom_bar(fill = "#b148d2") + theme_classic() + ggtitle("Common Eye Color Of Characters in Star Wars") + xlab("Eye Color") + ylab("Amount of Characters")
```

4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 
```{r}
library(jtools)
ggplot(starwars, aes(y=homeworld, x=height)) + geom_point() + theme_apa()
```

5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(y=homeworld, x=height)) + geom_point() + theme_apa() + ggtitle("Height of Characters per Homeworld") + xlab("Height of Characters") + ylab("Homeworld")

```


6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height)) + geom_point(na.rm=TRUE) + theme_apa()
```


7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height)) + geom_point(na.rm=TRUE) + theme_apa()+ ggtitle("Mass vs Height of Star Wars Characters") + xlab("Mass of Characters") + ylab("Height Of Characters")

```

8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color = gender)) + geom_point(na.rm=TRUE) + theme_apa()
```

9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}

ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color = gender)) + geom_point(na.rm=TRUE) + theme_apa()+ ggtitle("Mass vs Height of Star Wars Characters") + xlab("Mass of Characters") + ylab("Height Of Characters") 
```
